In the course of many of the peaceful opposition demonstrations, most of the applicants were arrested and subsequently convicted, as the assemblies had not been authorised.

The first, second, third, fifth and sixth applicants argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that they had been unlawfully arrested for their political activity, including their active participation in demonstrations.
The fourth applicant argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that he had been unlawfully arrested for the comments he had posted on social media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in unauthorised gatherings were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', emphasised that those who have called for public protest in Azerbaijan have been dealt with harshly, with criminal proceedings initiated against them under fabricated charges.

In a public statement of 7 March 2014, titled 'Azerbaijan: Opposition party loses HQ after explosion and sees seven members arrested within 2 weeks', Amnesty International reported on numerous detentions and arrests of activists of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan during late February and early March 2014.

State-funded lawyers were appointed to assist the applicants during the court proceedings before the first-instance courts.

According to the transcripts of the respective hearings, the State-funded lawyer for the fourth applicant, Ms S.H., briefly asked the court to consider the young age of the fourth applicant.

In their statements, the police officers questioned as witnesses reiterated the official version of the reasons for the applicants' arrests.
In the case of the third applicant, the court questioned three prosecution witnesses.

In the case of the sixth applicant, the court did not question any witnesses.
